The Manager, The Oriental Insurance Co. ... vs Sri.Bhimayya @ Bhimappa @ Dodda ... on 11 September, 2024
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51199921/
3

 Oral Judgment

(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA)
1.
The insurer as well as the claimants are in appeal.
2. The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.6,71,000/- for the death of one Hanumanthi, who was killed in an accident which occurred on 06.04.2014 when she was walking on the road.
3. The Tribunal has recorded a finding that Hanumanthi was indeed traveling on the road as a pedestrian when she was hit by the rider of the motorcycle which has been insured by the appellant.
4. The insurer, however, contends that all the police records, starting from the FIR till the laying of the charge sheet, clearly indicate that Hanumanthi was a pillion rider and not a pedestrian.
It is contended that since the motorcycle in question was covered only under a statutory policy, a deliberate attempt has been made to convert Hanumanthi from a pillion rider to a pedestrian.
It is submitted that the entire story put forward by the claimants was fraudulent and was designed to secure compensation.
6. The claimant, on the other hand, contends that the complaint was admittedly lodged by the father of the deceased, who was not an eye-witness.

7. It is contended that, if an investigation is started by the police on the statement of a person who is not an eyewitness, and the police arrive at a conclusion that the deceased was riding pillion, that would not bind the Tribunal.

8. The Tribunal has recorded a finding that Hanumanthi was a pedestrian on the basis of the evidence adduced of one Muniyamma, who was stated to be a co-employee of Hanumanthi in the coolie work that they had been engaged in.
The Tribunal has found no reason to disbelieve the evidence of Muniyamma and this Muniyamma was also cross
-examined in detail by the insurer and the insurer NC: 2024:KHC-K:6869 was not able to elicit any admission from her that Hanumanthi was a pillion rider.
9. In my view, this assessment of oral evidence by the Tribunal to arrive at the conclusion that Hanumanthi was a pillion rider, cannot be found fault with.

10. Learned counsel for the insurer presses into service the judgment rendered by the Supreme Court in the case of Oriental Insurance Company Limited Vs. Premlata Shukla and Others and National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Rattani and Others.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Chamundeswari and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. It is no doubt true that in Premlata Shukla's case, the Supreme Court did look into the FIR to record a finding.

However, it is to be noticed here that was a case NC: 2024:KHC-K:6869 in which,
the Supreme Court was dealing with a situation where an argument was sought to be advanced that,
only a part of the FIR was to be accepted and the other part, which was inconvenient to one party,
was not to be accepted.

In that context, the Supreme Court has held that once a document is admitted into evidence, the entire document will have to be taken into consideration and only a part of the document cannot be eschewed.

12. In the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Rattani, the Supreme Court was dealing with a case in which a truck was alleged to be carrying a marriage party of 22-30 persons but the claimants who were victims in the accident contended that, they were not gratuitous passengers, but were persons carrying with their goods.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Rattani
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that context, the Supreme Court, after noticing that the High Court therein, had not assessed the evidence, proceeded to examine the issue with reference to the FIR and record a finding.

It is therefore clear that the said decision cannot be made applicable to the facts of NC: 2024:KHC-K:6869 the present case, where an eye-witness was examined and who clearly stated that she was traveling along with the deceased in the road, when the deceased was hit by a motorcycle.
13. In the light of the factual situation involved in this case, the Tribunal was justified in recording of finding that the accident did take place.

14. It may also be noticed here that when the insurer took up the plea that no accident occurred and wanted to rely upon the police records, nothing prevented the insurer from summoning the investigating officers, the panch witnesses and also the owner and driver of the offending motorcycle, to establish their case.

The insurer, having not taken the pains to discharge the burden that it had cast upon itself regarding the deceased being a pillion rider, it cannot thereafter turn around and rely upon the police documents to put forward to support its contention.

It is settled law that an FIR, a charge sheet and statements recorded by the police during the cross-investigation, are NC: 2024:KHC-K:6869 not conclusive pieces of evidence and they are nevertheless required to be proved in a manner provided under the Evidence Act.

The argument of the insurer that every statement in the FIR, charge sheet or the statements recorded while doing a course of investigation should be accepted as gospel truth, cannot be a legally sustainable argument.
In the result, the appeal of the insurer is dismissed.
15. As far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the claimant was aged about 33 years and was stated to be a Coolie since there was no proof of income.
16. The notional income of Rs.7,500/- will have to be applied for the accidents of the year 2014 as determined by the KSLSA.
To this sum future prospects of 40% will have to be added.

Out of the said notional income, 1/3rd will have to be deducted and the net income would be Rs.7,000/- per The Manager, The Oriental Insurance Co. ... vs Sri.Bhimayya @ Bhimappa @ Dodda ... on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51199921/
5 month.

The claimant No.1 being the husband alone, would be entitled to a sum of Rs.15,12,000/-
(Rs.7,000x12x18) towards 'loss of dependency'.
18.
In addition, he would also be entitled to sum Rs.44,000/- towards 'loss of consortium' and Rs.33,000/- under the 'conventional heads'.

19. Consequently, the claimant is entitled for the following sums:
 Sl. Amount
Heads of Compensation  No. (in Rs.)
1. Loss of Dependency 15,12,000  2. Loss of Consortium 44,000  3. Conventional Head 33,000

20 . The respondent No.3 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded along with interest within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

The entire amount awarded by the Tribunal shall be invested in a fixed deposit for a period of ten years and the husband would be entitled to withdraw only the interest that accrues on the said amount.

22. An argument was also advanced, that the driver of the vehicle did not possess a driving licence,
and this was established by the fact that the owner of the vehicle did not respond to the notice issued by the insurer.

If the insurer is of the view that there was a breach of the policy conditions, it would be open for the insurer to initiate appropriate proceedings against the owner of the vehicle and establish the breach and recover the compensation that it is required to pay pursuant to the award passed by this court.
